message.content:
Sure! Below is everything you’ll need to post your comment (`{"type":"comment","attributes":{"text":"Confirmed #malware"}}`) to the IP `192.168.1.1` on VirusTotal using your API key `ABC321`.

---

### 1️⃣ What’s happening?

* **Endpoint** – `POST https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/<IP>/comments`
* **Auth Header** – `X‑Apikey: <YOUR_API_KEY>`
* **Body** – Your JSON payload exactly as you supplied.

If you’re calling the newer V3 API, the auth header name is `X‑Apikey`.  
(Older “V2” endpoints used `api_key=` query param.)

---

### 2️⃣ Quick one‑liner with *curl*

```bash
curl -s \
     --request POST \
     --url https://www.virustool.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments \
     --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --header "X-Apikey: ABC321" \
     --data '{"type":"comment","attributes":{"text":"Confirmed #malware"}}'
```

Replace `https://www.virustool.com/...` with the actual base URL if needed.

---

### 3️⃣ Full Python example (requests)

```python
import requests
import json

BASE_URL   = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3"
IP_ADDRESS = "192.168.1.1"

payload = {
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": { "text": "Confirmed #malware" }
}

headers = {
    "Accept":        "application/json",
    "Content-type":  "application/json",
    "X-Apikey":      "ABC321"          # <-- YOUR API KEY HERE
}

response = requests.post(
    f"{BASE_URL}/ip_addresses/{IP_ADDRESS}/comments",
    headers=headers,
    data=json.dumps(payload)
)

print("Status:", response.status_code)
print("Response body:")
print(response.json())
```

Make sure you’ve installed the `requests` library first:

```bash
pip install requests
```

---

### 4️⃣ Things to double‑check

| ✅ Item | Why |
|---------|-----|
| Correct IP | Must match the exact IP you intend to annotate |
| Endpoint Path | `/ip_addresses/<IP>/comments` |
| Auth Header | `X-Apikey`, not `Authorization` unless you prefer bearer token style |
| Payload Structure | Exactly `"type":"comment"` + `"attributes":{"text":"…"}"` |

---

#### 🎉 Success!

When the request succeeds, you’ll receive a `201 Created` status along with details of the newly created comment object. If there’s an error, the HTTP status code and accompanying JSON will explain what went wrong—most commonly authentication issues or malformed payloads.
